newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends down near three-month low vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends down near three-month low vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down near a three-month low at 8.2990 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2965 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on speculative selling ahead of the close, traders said.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2968.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2965 and consolidated around that level for most of the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2960 before it fell in late trade, hitting a low of 8.2995.
Trading was active with most done at about 8.2965, traders said.
Dealers said speculative selling pushed the yuan sharply down before the end of the session, though the currency consolidated around at 8.2965 for most of the trade.
"The yuan will rebound in the short term to reverse today's losses," one dealer said.
A second dealer said the yuan's downward trend gradually became clear after the day's falls which indicated it had finished its consolidation between 8.2950 and 8.2960 over the past few weeks.
He added that no intervention by the central bank was seen in the market.
The dollar's fluctuation in the world market because of the rise in the U.S. interest rate seemed have little impact on the yuan's movement, traders said.
They said they expected the yuan to rebound on Thursday.
The yuan ended up at 6.7000 from 6.7440 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0713 from 1.0710 against the Hong Kong dollar.
